newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans see budget/tax deal soon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans see budget/tax deal soon.

text.p: Senate Republican leaders said Monday they hope to conclude a spending and tax cut deal with the White House "in the next couple of hours" and that four issues remained to be resolved.

One of the unsettled issues involves a possible $24 billion program to provide health care to 2.2 million uninsured children. Republicans want President Clinton to agree to give states more flexibility to decide which health benefits will be covered.

"We are very close to reaching an agreement, but as we said before, until the last piece is agreed to and signed off on none of it is completely closed. We hope to be able to do that shortly, sometime in the next hour or two hopefully," Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told reporters.
Lott and other Republican leaders held a brief news conference as they met to discuss the outlook.
Republican aides said changes in the tax cut proposal have resulted in a net tax cut that could be above $90 billion over five years. The had hoped it would reach $85 billion.
Other than the disagreement over children's health care coverage, the Republicans declined to discuss publicly the outstanding issues still being negotiated.

Lott and Republicans from House and Senate continued talks with White House officials who included Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, Budget Director Franklin Raines, Clinton's Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles and his economic adviser Gene Sperling.
